raw_case_text:
A 47-year-old male presented to our institution complaining of a 1-month history of abdominal pain. His medical history was significant for HIV (diagnosed 18 years ago), KS, and chronic left-leg edema secondary to pelvic infiltration of KS, compressing the common femoral and superficial femoral veins for which he previously received chemotherapy (paclitaxel, doxorubicin, and then gemcitabine) and electron beam radiation. The patient also noted worsening abdominal distention, which he attributed to his worsening abdominal pain. In addition to his abdominal distension, he gave a history of unintentional 4.5 kg (10 lbs) weight loss over a 1-week period and bilateral lower-extremity edema that was worse on the left side. He also complained of progressively worsening dyspnea, nausea, intermittent pyrexia as high as 38.3 C (101 F), anorexia, rhinorrhea, and malaise for 2 days prior to admission. He admitted to being compliant with his current antiretroviral regimen, which included raltegravir, ritonavir, and the combination abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine.
On admission, his blood pressure was 113/77 mm Hg, pulse 97 beats per minute, temperature 36.5 C (97.7 F), respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, and pulse oximetry 99% (room air). Physical examination was significant for generalized abdominal distension on inspection, decreased frequency of bowel sounds, and generalized tenderness to palpation without any rebound tenderness or guarding. He had bilateral flank dullness to percussion, positive shifting dullness, and fluid thrill. There was no cervical, axillary, epitrochlear, and inguinal adenopathy. HIV serology showed an absolute CD4 count of 261 cells/microl and a quantitative HIV-1 RNA level of 220 copies/ml. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was significant for moderate-volume abdominal ascites prominently seen in the perihepatic region extending into the right paracolic gutter without any evidence of bowel obstruction (fig. 1). His ascites rapidly reaccumulated within 48 h after the initial paracentesis.
His initial ultrasound-guided paracentesis yielded 1,365 ml cloudy, yellow ascitic fluid. Analysis of the ascitic fluid was positive for a large number of atypical lymphoid cells. Flow cytometry cytospin showed pleomorphic, large lymphoid cells with large nuclei, multiple prominent nucleoli, and deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a plasmacytoid appearance. Polymerase chain reaction showed clonal B cells, and HHV-8 immunostain revealed positive nuclear staining (fig. 2), which confirmed the diagnosis of PEL. The cell block preparation revealed multiple malignant lymphocytes (fig. 3).
Given his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance score of 1, he was promptly started on DA-EPOCH as we were optimistic of a good outcome. His ascites gradually improved and did not recur on follow-up visits after 4 cycles of DA-EPOCH.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old HIV-positive male with a history of Kaposi sarcoma presented with a 1-month history of worsening abdominal pain and abdominal distension, a 1-week history of 4.5 kg (10-lb) weight loss, and a 2-day history of dyspnea, nausea, intermittent fever up to 38.3 °C, anorexia, rhinorrhea, and malaise.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the month preceding admission, the patient experienced progressively worsening generalized abdominal pain and abdominal distension, accompanied by a 4.5 kg weight loss over the prior week, asymmetric bilateral lower extremity edema (left worse than right), and 2 days of worsening dyspnea, nausea, anorexia, rhinorrhea, malaise, and intermittent fever up to 38.3 °C (101 °F).
subjective.past_medical_history: 18-year history of HIV infection (adherent to raltegravir, ritonavir, and abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine); cutaneous/pelvic Kaposi sarcoma complicated by chronic left femoral vein compression and left leg lymphedema/edema, previously treated with systemic paclitaxel, doxorubicin, gemcitabine, and electron-beam radiotherapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for abdominal pain, abdominal distension, 4.5 kg weight loss in 1 week, asymmetric leg edema, dyspnea, nausea, anorexia, intermittent fever (38.3 °C), rhinorrhea, and malaise. Home medications: raltegravir, ritonavir, and abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine (Trizivir).

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: blood pressure 113/77 mmHg, pulse 97 beats/min, temperature 36.5 °C (97.7 °F), respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, and SpO2 99% on room air; ECOG performance status 1. Abdominal examination revealed marked distension, hypoactive bowel sounds, diffuse tenderness without rebound or guarding, bilateral flank dullness, shifting dullness, and a positive fluid thrill, along with chronic asymmetric left-predominant lower extremity edema and no peripheral lymphadenopathy.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission absolute CD4+ T-cell count was 261 cells/µL. Abdominal and pelvic CT demonstrated moderate-volume perihepatic and right paracolic ascites without bowel obstruction or solid lymphomatous masses. Ultrasound-guided paracentesis (1,365 mL cloudy yellow fluid, rapidly reaccumulating within 48 hours) with cytology, cell block, flow cytometry, PCR clonality, and immunohistochemistry revealed numerous large pleomorphic plasmacytoid lymphoid cells with deeply basophilic cytoplasm, multiple prominent nucleoli, clonal B-cell Ig rearrangement by PCR, and positive nuclear HHV-8 immunostaining.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Peritoneal extracavitary/classic HHV-8-positive primary effusion lymphoma (PEL) presenting with rapidly reaccumulating malignant ascites in a 47-year-old male with well-controlled HIV-1 infection (plasma HIV-1 RNA 220 copies/mL, CD4+ count 261 cells/µL on raltegravir, ritonavir, and abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine) and prior pelvic Kaposi sarcoma. Confirmed via ascitic fluid cytology, clonal B-cell PCR, and nuclear HHV-8 immunohistochemistry. Prompt initiation of systemic dose-adjusted EPOCH (DA-EPOCH) chemotherapy alongside continued ART resulted in complete resolution of ascites without recurrence after 4 cycles.
